doc.title: Kenny Burrell — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Blue Lights for Blue Note, Warhol covers and Tina Brooks
summary: Lion wanted rehearsals for Blue Note sessions; Burrell recalls the covers and Tina Brooks.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: I have another one here, "Blue Lights Vol. I and II" since these seem to be companion. We'll talk about this one. Its from '58.

Those were a different kind of blowing session. Those were for Blue Note. Alfred Lion really liked to have a little rehearsal. He didn't like to take too many chances on stuff. You'd bring in some songs but if at all possible he'd like to have at least one rehearsal. Even if it was going to be an hour before the date he liked to have them maybe the day before or something like that, but even if it was sometime before they started recording he wanted to make sure you guys rehearsed the stuff to make sure the lines were together. One of the things outstanding about those two records is those are Andy Warhol Covers. This is before Andy Warhol was really expensive, he was affordable then and both of them are Andy Warhol covers. The designer was Reid...I'm not sure.
Yeah, so they were able to get some Warhol covers. Are these Art Blakey and Bobby Timmons and all that?
Ok. Those are the blowing sessions for Blue Note, which are great, and one of my unsung heroes, besides Junior Cook, is the other tenor player from the Bronx.
I loved him. I loved his sound and his feeling. He was quite-­
Louis Smith is on here on trumpet.

Yeah Louis Smith, I guess its Dr. Louis Smith now? He was at Michigan for a while. Yeah he was a newcomer on the scene then. I think Lee Morgan is on one of them, maybe, maybe not that one. Oh no, Lee Morgan is on one of the ones I did with Jimmy Smith. Same kind of sessions.
